post.caption: This burial suit has 2,498 jade pieces. It belonged to Liu Sheng, who lived in China's Han dynasty, and army engineers found his tomb by chance in 1968. It was the first complete jade suit ever found, and before that suits were known only from old texts. Gold wire weighing about 1,100 grams joins the pieces, and each jade tile has holes at its corners for the wire. Jade was believed to keep a body from decaying. Making one may have taken about ten years. His wife Dou Wan's suit has 2,160 pieces. Liu Sheng's suit is kept at the Hebei Museum in Shijiazhuang.
